judged_text: The new automatic-group guard tests for add_members (line 83), remove_member (line 104), and update (line 51) all hardcode `group_id: 1` / `id: 1` and assume the seeded automatic group occupies id 1, instead of Fabricating an automatic group the way the .destroy tests in this same diff do. If automatic-group seeding in the test database ever changes (ids shift, seeds not loaded), these tests silently exercise a non-automatic group — add_members with the fake username 'l77t' would then silently succeed and the 422 assertion would fail confusingly, or worse, the remove_member assertion would guard the wrong group — and the failure message points nowhere near the real cause.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s controller specs do hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` for automatic-group cases instead of fabricating an automatic group. Specifically: in `.update` spec: `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` then `Group.find(1)`; in `.add_members` spec: `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...`; and in `.remove_member` spec: `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...` (also note it uses PUT even though the route/controller action expects DELETE). This makes the tests depend on an assumption that an automatic group exists with ID 1, unlike the `.destroy` tests which explicitly `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`. That’s a real, diff-grounded test fragility/incorrect setup issue rather than an application behavior defect.
